editorial:
If you love a creepy slow burn that keeps you guessing, The Boy delivers a fun, unsettling ride. Lauren Cohan plays Greta, an American nanny who arrives at a remote English estate to care for what she thinks is a child. Instead, she finds a porcelain doll named Brahms and a strict list of rules from his odd owners. The atmosphere is quiet and eerie, with long hallways and creaky rooms that make you want to look over your shoulder. The story leans on mystery more than gore, so it works well for viewers who prefer suspense over jump scares.

The acting is solid, especially Cohan carrying most scenes alone with the doll. Pacing starts slow but builds nicely toward a wild final act. Some twists feel predictable if you have seen similar horror films, and a few plot holes might bug picky viewers. Still, it is a great pick for a spooky movie night. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final act, Greta discovers the doll is not alive. The real Brahms, now a grown man, has been living inside the walls of the house. He killed his parents years ago and uses the doll as a cover. Greta fights him off, escapes with Malcolm, and they drive away. The last shot shows the doll's head turning slightly, leaving a creepy hint that the nightmare might not be over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creepy doll horror and slow-burn mysteries.
